romans-10-study-notes.summary: Israel was rejected due to not feeling a need for salvation, being zealous for God through self-made traditions, and being proud and self-righteous, along with misunderstanding the law.
key_points: Did not feel need for salvation; thought they were fine, save themselves.
Zealous for God; made own traditions and worshipped them.
Proud and self-righteous; refused to listen and learn.
Misunderstood their own law; law leads to the savior, not just outward obedience.
sections: Israel rejections — Reasons for their rejection 1-13

related.title: Foundation of Dedication
related.why: This note contrasts the self-made traditions mentioned in the 'Reasons for Rejection' by emphasizing offering the body, mind, and will as sacrifices to God.

related.title: Honest Self-Evaluation
related.why: This note relates to the 'proud and self-righteous' aspect of rejection by instructing Christians to honestly assess their spiritual gifts without under- or over-evaluating themselves.

related.title: God's Perfect Plan
related.why: This note provides a contrasting perspective to the rejection by asserting that God is always at work with a perfect plan for those who love Him, regardless of past failures.

romans-10-study-notes.summary: The remedy for rejection involves a missionary program, questioning the interchangeability of believing and obeying, and emphasizing that one must first hear.
key_points: Used for missionary program.
Is believing and obeying interchangeable?
To believe one must first hear.

related.title: Reasons for Rejection

related.title: God's Perfect Plan
related.why: This note provides the ultimate assurance that underpins the hope necessary for overcoming rejection.

romans-10-study-notes.summary: Israel is guilty because they did hear, which allows the message to be shared with the Gentiles, and God still yearns for His people.
key_points: Israel is guilty; Israel DID hear.
Message is shared with Gentiles due to Israel rejection.
God still yearns for His people.

related.title: God's Perfect Plan

romans-12-study-notes.summary: Dedication involves offering the body, mind, and will as sacrifices to God, rooted in the context of God's work in the world.
key_points: Body as a living sacrifice.
Mind as a sacrifice, changed by the Holy Spirit.
Will as a sacrifice, yielding to God's will through prayer.

Dedication - 3 steps > Your mind is a sacrifice to God
Dedication - 3 steps > Your will is a sacrifice to God

related.title: God's Perfect Plan

related.title: Hope and Faith
related.why: Hope and faith are the necessary emotional and spiritual anchors that sustain the dedication to God.

related.title: Reasons for Rejection
related.why: Knowing the reasons for rejection highlights the urgency and necessity of offering the body, mind, and will as sacrifice.

romans-12-study-notes.summary: Christians must honestly assess their spiritual gifts and ministries without under- or over-evaluating themselves, as both are forms of pride.
key_points: Identify spiritual gifts and ministries.
Be honest in self-evaluation.
Avoid under or over-evaluation.

related.title: Foundation of Dedication
related.why: This note provides the framework for how one should offer their gifts and self in service, which is central to honest self-evaluation.

related.title: Faithful Cooperation

related.title: Loving Participation
related.why: This note defines the character of love required in participation, which is the standard against which one should honestly measure their own spiritual state.

romans-12-study-notes.summary: Cooperation with others requires working together regardless of personal feelings, recognizing that all gifts are tools for building.
key_points: Work with others even if you don't like them.
No gift is better or greater than another.
Gifts are tools to build with.

related.title: Foundation of Dedication

related.title: Loving Participation

related.title: Relationship to Enemies
related.why: This note provides a specific example of how cooperation and love are applied when interacting with opposition.

romans-12-study-notes.summary: Loving participation involves maintaining an honest, humble love characterized by joy in hope, patience in affliction, and faithfulness in prayer.
key_points: Attitude matters in love.
Love is the circulatory system of the spiritual body.
Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, and faithful in prayer.

related.title: Foundation of Dedication

related.title: Faithful Cooperation

related.title: Relationship to Enemies
related.why: This note illustrates the practical application of loving participation by showing how to respond to opposition with love instead of revenge.

romans-12-study-notes.summary: Returning good for evil requires love, contrasting impatience with the way Christ follows love rather than seeking revenge.
key_points: Return good in exchange for evil requires love.
Difference between impatience/lack of love and following Christ.
View justice as love.

related.title: Loving Participation

related.title: Faithful Cooperation

romans-08-study-notes.summary: Romans 8 covers four spiritual freedoms: freedom from judgment, freedom from defeat, freedom from discouragement, and freedom from separation.
key_points: Freedom from judgment (No condemnation).
Freedom from defeat (Submit to God because we cannot save ourselves).
Freedom from discouragement (No frustration).
Freedom from separation.

related.why: This note provides the ultimate context for the freedom from defeat, showing that God's plan encompasses and secures the freedom believers possess.

related.title: Hope and Faith
related.why: This note details the source of hope, which is intrinsically linked to the freedom from separation and the assurance of God's perfect plan.

romans-08-study-notes.summary: Suffering is a result of Adam’s sin but is not useless; creation groans, believers groan, and the Holy Spirit groans, yet there is freedom from discouragement.
key_points: Creation groans because of Adam’s sin, but suffering is not useless.
Embrace today’s sufferings to build up to tomorrow.
Everyone suffers, but solutions vary.
Believers groan, tasting glory and anxious for it.

romans-08-study-notes.summary: Believers have hope because they know the climax of adoption is coming, and faith is the assurance of things hoped for.
key_points: Believers have hope as the climax of adoption is coming.
Adoption begins when saved, conversion when the Spirit of adoption comes.
Faith is the assurance of things hoped for and the conviction of things not seen.
